messages.subject: more distance sampling references
parts:
Dear list,

The webpage with pdf's of papers and reports related to
distance sampling that I keep online at

http://www.creem.st-and.ac.uk/tiago/webpages/distance_pdfs.htm

has reached more than 100 references, with over 5000 visits since it
started. Thanks for those who have contributed for it.

I've decided to put online a new bibliographic list on distance
sampling, available at

http://www.creem.st-and.ac.uk/tiago/webpages/distbiblio.html

It contains over 600 references on work done with or about distance
sampling (important: these are not online as pdf's; in fact, I've not
yet combined the two lists, i.e., there might be papers online as pdf's
that I have not included in the new reference list - a TO DO for the
future,). If you happen to
look at it, please let me know if you have any suggestions, new entries,
corrections for existing ones, etc.

In such a large amount of references it is likely that there might be
some errors (in the next weeks I'll probably correct many minor typos
etc), so double check any info you use from it - I take no
responsibility for it's use.

It is not a complete list, but references
I've collected from several sources and also as result of my own web
searching activities.

For those of you with new PhD, MSc, etc students in topics related to
distance sampling, this might be a good way of introducing them to the
bibliography in the area. If you do so, please tell your students to
contact me if they find any errors or mistakes.

A note about the hiperlinks on the new bibliographic list page: they are
dead, and just a nuisance, resulting from the conversion from TeX to
HTML. If someone knows how to deal with it I would greatly apreciate a hi=
nt.

I hope this might be helpful to some of you. If it is, let me know...
it's always good to know.

Tiago
